adversary: passive network observer
threat: traffic analysis of relay delivery
residual_risk: global passive observer timing correlation remains without anonymity transports

adversary: active MITM at first contact
threat: substituted ContactDescriptor/keys
residual_risk: trust-on-first-use until manual/continuity verification

adversary: malicious relay
threat: correlating stable queue identifiers
residual_risk: per-relay timing/volume

adversary: malicious directory
threat: split identity views/equivocation
residual_risk: no global transparency root in v1

adversary: malicious storage provider
threat: blob deletion or corruption
residual_risk: availability loss without redundancy

adversary: compromised SFU/TURN
threat: media decryption/injection
residual_risk: call metadata to media provider

adversary: colluding providers
threat: cross-provider correlation
residual_risk: collusion defeats provider separation

adversary: hostile modified client / spammer
threat: introduction floods
residual_risk: Sybil identities are cheap; reach is bounded

adversary: malicious admin within permissions
threat: abuse of legitimate grants
residual_risk: legitimate authority can be misused; fork/leave remains

adversary: compromised control device
threat: seizing account via quarantine/promotion
residual_risk: single-controller accounts are taken over by one compromise

adversary: stale backup/provider rollback
threat: resurrecting revoked devices/policies
residual_risk: isolated device without gossip may be partitioned

adversary: recovery provider/guardians
threat: recovery becoming a master key
residual_risk: guardian collusion at configured threshold

adversary: active attacker/provider
threat: CryptoProfile stripping downgrade
residual_risk: first contact with no established floor

adversary: concurrent group members
threat: same-epoch MLS fork or policy/MLS divergence
residual_risk: coordinator liveness under partition

adversary: mirrored key providers
threat: one-time key split-brain
residual_risk: last-resort key reuse under depletion

adversary: hostile sender content
threat: parser/decoder exploitation via media, packs or rich text
residual_risk: platform decoder zero-days

adversary: attacker URL
threat: link-preview SSRF/rebinding
residual_risk: preview fetch reveals recipient activity unless proxied

adversary: compromised build/update infrastructure
threat: malicious release
residual_risk: targeted store-signed builds remain hard to detect

adversary: malicious/compromised PWA origin
threat: malicious JavaScript from the ClientHost origin
residual_risk: browser platform cannot prevent a compromised origin; native is higher assurance

adversary: single cloud vendor (policy, filter, outage, coercion)
threat: vendor-wide disabling of OM Homes (monoculture)
residual_risk: relationships whose every route is on one vendor lose routes until re-homing

adversary: hosting-account attacker (phished cloud credentials)
threat: deploying malicious ClientHost code for one user
residual_risk: targeted substitution detectable only by independent observation

adversary: proximate adversary (partner/family/employer)
threat: silently linking an extra device
residual_risk: notice depends on victim seeing another device

adversary: coercive adversary (seizure, compelled unlock, border)
threat: reading an unlocked device
residual_risk: unlocked device reveals retained data; no deniability promised

adversary: OS/cloud backup service or its compromiser
threat: plaintext/key copies in device backups
residual_risk: platforms without exclusion controls

adversary: OS snapshot/screen capture consumers
threat: app-switcher snapshots/screenshots
residual_risk: PWA cannot suppress snapshots

adversary: keyboard/writing-tool vendors
threat: IME learning or cloud spellcheck upload
residual_risk: OS-level tools may ignore page hints

adversary: malicious or over-privileged browser extension
threat: reading the decrypted DOM
residual_risk: cannot be prevented by a web page; disclosed

adversary: other users of a shared device
threat: cross-user access on one OS account
residual_risk: shared OS account is not a private place

adversary: future quantum/cryptanalytic attacker recording traffic
threat: harvest-now-decrypt-later against classical v1 MLS
residual_risk: v1 group traffic recorded before PQ migration stays exposed

adversary: prompt-injecting content
threat: LLM tool misuse or escalation
residual_risk: granted capabilities can still be misused within scope

adversary: malicious plugin
threat: ambient authority or exfiltration
residual_risk: granted plaintext-read plus user-approved egress

adversary: malicious bridge/foreign network
threat: spoofed foreign identity, loops, reflection
residual_risk: bridge sees plaintext by design

adversary: hostile archive/importer
threat: authority cloning or fabricated history via import
residual_risk: imported history is only as honest as its source

adversary: steward/business capture or disappearance
threat: project governance becoming protocol authority
residual_risk: founder-only S0 custody until co-stewards exist

adversary: unpatched implementations / uncoordinated disclosure
threat: exploitation of known vulnerabilities without a kill switch
residual_risk: unupdated peers remain vulnerable; peers see 'needs update'

adversary: resource-exhausting attacker
threat: denial of service by quota exhaustion
residual_risk: free tiers fail closed; availability loss

adversary: impersonator
threat: confusable names/copied avatars
residual_risk: users may ignore warnings

adversary: self-verifying design author/agent
threat: evidence that only confirms its author's assumptions
residual_risk: independent reviewers may share blind spots

adversary: impersonator of an abandoned account / stale route
threat: messages sent to a dead or hijacked abandoned identity
residual_risk: unretired lost accounts look merely offline

adversary: abusers of public surfaces
threat: illegal content hosted on public Publications/catalogs/blob hosts
residual_risk: private E2EE content is not scanned by design

adversary: attacker holding a recovery custodian (phished platform account, found recovery key, colluding guardians)
threat: takeover through default recovery
residual_risk: a user with no remaining device cannot veto within the delay; the attacker wins that race. Disclosed in the ContinuityAssessment.

adversary: attacker who compromises a T1 host's hosting account
threat: malicious ClientHost JavaScript served to every member of a community Home
residual_risk: members who explicitly opt into the host's ClientHost inherit the host's account security

adversary: attacker holding a recovery custodian
threat: repeated recovery requests to exhaust the user's vigilance (veto fatigue)
residual_risk: notices repeat until the user rotates custody; rotation is guided after the first veto

adversary: a compromised or mistaken design agent, or a tampered zip
threat: silent regression or malicious change introduced through an imported design drop
residual_risk: the validator catches contract violations, not every semantic regression; the operator must review each drop's merge diff

adversary: platform credential-manager vendor or observer
threat: synced-passkey custody reveals that a platform account uses an OM distribution
residual_risk: the credential manager sees the OM RP ID, random RecoveryHandle, human recovery locator in WebAuthn user.name and its own telemetry; random user.id prevents direct AccountID encoding but does not guarantee unlinkability (ADR-0141)

adversary: phished or compromised recovery custodian
threat: custodian alone permanently revokes controllers or retires the account with no delay or veto
residual_risk: a user with no live device and a compromised custodian loses the race (T-041)

adversary: stolen messaging device or colluding guardians
threat: a successor pointer redirects every relationship to an attacker account while the owner keeps working devices
residual_risk: a constitutional majority (or recovery vote after delay without veto) can still move the account

adversary: malicious directory, publisher or IntroGate
threat: substitutes the intro identity or request key, or learns the sender's identity from the first-contact request
residual_risk: trust-on-first-use without key transparency until safety-number verification; IntroGate sees timing, size and network address

adversary: quarantined or stolen device
threat: publishes a newer RelaySet or BlobLocationRecord pointing at attacker queues, blackholing delivery and collecting metadata
residual_risk: a peer that has not yet seen the quarantine may accept one set until it syncs control state

adversary: anyone who learns a device id; KeyMaterialProvider
asset: one-time forward secrecy and account unlinkability
threat: drains one-time prekey pools and correlates repeated fetches for the same stable DeviceID
residual_risk: AsyncKeyBundle v1 no longer exposes an account-wide ACS generation/hash correlator, but subject_device_id remains a stable per-device correlator and timing/inventory shape can still link activity for that device; rate limits and relationship-scoped fetch capabilities bound abuse but cannot make a provider oblivious to the device it serves.

adversary: spammer claiming referrals
threat: forged referrals consume the R-195 reserved queue
residual_risk: a contact who leaks tokens can admit strangers up to the tokens issued

adversary: network attacker or hostile peer arguing compatibility
threat: forces a downgrade through an undefined floor exception or by comparing profile ids
residual_risk: a forged SecurityAdvisory is bounded by advisory signature rules (ADR-0104) and never lowers the generation

adversary: device seizer, coercer or any member holding decrypted group messages
threat: MLS leaf signatures chaining to AccountID let a third party verify group transcripts of other members' messages
residual_risk: inherent to RFC 9420 authentication in OM v1; ADR-0138 closes deniability as a documented non-goal unless a separate future research CryptoProfile is adopted.

adversary: offline, lost or malicious CommitCoordinator device
asset: liveness of security reductions (revocation, removal, leave)
threat: coordinator delays or censors removal of a compromised device, a member, or itself
residual_risk: a revoked device keeps receiving group secrets for up to sequencing_timeout plus propagation delay

adversary: spammer or stranger who is (or befriends) a group member
threat: unsolicited group add or KeyPackage harvest reveals the invitee's AccountID and devices to every member; a leaked invite link outlives its issuer
residual_risk: an accepted invitee's identity is visible to all members by design

adversary: Room member, full-room service or bridge not joined to a call, colluding with an untrusted SFU
threat: a non-joined Room endpoint or untrusted SFU obtains group-call media keys and silently listens to streams
residual_risk: joined participants legitimately receive media keys and can record/re-share plaintext; traffic metadata at the SFU remains outside media-content confidentiality

adversary: holder of a compromised Publication signing key; withholding mirror
asset: integrity of a public Publication feed
threat: backdated posts signed after revocation verify as pre-revocation; mirrors withhold revocations and tombstones
residual_risk: a subscriber that never sees the revocation keeps accepting the key's posts; withholding delays but cannot roll back a seen head

adversary: group member who creates a GroupHistoryBundle
asset: authenticity of pre-join history shown to newcomers
threat: bundle author invents or alters other members' past messages
residual_risk: newcomers must trust the bundle author for content; the UI attributes it to that author

adversary: relay or delivery provider
asset: group membership and Room identity privacy
threat: raw MLS messages expose group_id and epoch, letting relays link copies across recipients and providers and possibly learn the ConversationID
residual_risk: timing and size correlation remain; a group_broadcast provider sees recipient-set linkage by declaration

adversary: malicious or compromised local plugin, or a local LLM running as one
threat: extension code sends events that recipients see as authored by the account with no human review
residual_risk: a user who confirms content they did not read closely still authors it

adversary: one Room member's personal plugin, service or automation
asset: confidentiality of other members' Room plaintext
threat: continuous export of Room plaintext on one member's local grant, invisible to other members
residual_risk: a member can still copy or screenshot manually; a modified client ignores taint (absolute rule 11)

adversary: holder of a briefly accessed or stolen messaging device
threat: minting RepresentationGrants that let a service post as 'Alice · via X' or receive counterparties' messages without their knowledge
residual_risk: a stolen control device can issue grants until quarantined; other devices see the notice

adversary: attacker holding a compromised service endpoint key
asset: confidentiality of Rooms where the service is installed
threat: revoked endpoint keeps receiving Room plaintext because no member learns of or commits its removal
residual_risk: exposure until the first member receives the head plus sequencing_timeout (ADR-0122 rule 8)

adversary: operator of a shared ClientHost, or an attacker who compromises its hosting account
asset: endpoint integrity of every user it serves
threat: malicious JavaScript served to all T0/T1 PWA users of a shared origin
residual_risk: a fully compromised origin can serve targeted code the digest check misses (CLIENTHOST §3); native clients remain the higher-assurance path

adversary: holder of the canonical release signing root, or anyone who coerces it
threat: canonical root used as a push-code channel into every self-hosted origin
residual_risk: an owner who pins the canonical root still trusts it, bounded by transparency and delay

adversary: Homes, PushGateways or the platform push service
threat: one platform token or Web Push endpoint handed to two parties links the profiles
residual_risk: on native a single token remains a declared linkage point unless vendor push is disabled per profile

adversary: attacker who controls the passkey provider account and obtains a copy of the browser profile
threat: one synced passkey both wraps the DeviceVault and is the RecoveryRoot, so it unseals local state
residual_risk: where only a synced passkey exists the at-rest boundary is reduced and stated

adversary: author of a theme or imported font
threat: glyph remapping makes a safety number, URL, label or prompt render differently from its string; malformed font exploits the parser
residual_risk: font sanitizers have had bugs; built-in fonts on reserved surfaces remove the spoofing channel there only

adversary: malicious plugin or mini-app in the PWA
asset: OM Core secrets and security prompts
threat: Spectre-class read of Core wasm memory from same-site code, or a mini-app drawing fake recovery/passkey prompts
residual_risk: depends on browser site isolation; plugins with content access are disabled where it is absent

adversary: T0 sponsor, or the operator/attacker of a single project-run PWA origin
threat: the origin that serves a T0 user's client code is chosen implicitly (the sponsor's, or one project origin for most users), making that party part of every such user's endpoint trust base
residual_risk: a user who explicitly opts into the sponsor's app server trusts the sponsor like their device; a compromised shared origin can still target individuals until the digest check notices

adversary: attacker controlling a template repository branch, a build-time dependency, or a stolen provisioning OAuth token
asset: code running in users' Homes and T2 ClientHosts
threat: provisioning activates code from a mutable branch outside the release trust root, or an account-wide token replaces the user's Workers
residual_risk: a compromised verifier release or release root is bounded by threshold roots and transparency, not eliminated

adversary: thief of a distribution's online advisory key, or a dominant distribution
asset: reachability between users of different distributions and profiles
threat: a malicious or compromised floor-raising SecurityAdvisory puts every relationship with other profiles or generations into 'Needs update', or forces a single-implementation profile
residual_risk: a compromised release root threshold can still sign a harmful floor until rotated; users keep override on non-threshold floors

adversary: operator of a Home running the discovery publisher, IntroGate and mailbox together (cloud vendor, T1 host or T0 sponsor)
asset: unlinkability of a user's published contact identity from mailbox activity; contact graph
threat: links the published identity to every deposit and drain, and observes contact edges among co-resident users
residual_risk: declared, not prevented: users who need separation must place the roles with different operators

adversary: sponsor who is a proximate adversary (partner, parent, employer)
asset: privacy of inbound contact and availability of the invitee's mailbox
threat: sponsor watches message timing and co-resident contacts, or revokes the mailbox to coerce or isolate the invitee
residual_risk: the sponsor sees timing for as long as the mailbox is used; the overlap window and early second route bound isolation, not observation

adversary: state or network operator
threat: network-level blocking of vendor IP ranges, SNI/hostnames or protocol fingerprints while the vendor keeps serving
residual_risk: a powerful censor can block every known path; OM makes no resilience claim before PR-013

adversary: state or network operator, forge or app store
threat: blocking a discovery suffix (for example workers.dev locators and invite pages), or removing the reference client from a forge or store
residual_risk: first contact through a blocked suffix fails until another locator or an out-of-band invite is used

adversary: a contact who is an estranged partner, ex-employer or stalker
threat: detects the user's presence on a shared LAN by matching relationship-derived rendezvous tags
residual_risk: a contact the user has marked can still detect co-presence by design

adversary: passive Wi-Fi observer
asset: unlinkability and contact-count privacy on a LAN
threat: counts per-contact tags to learn contact count, and links a tag set rotating together from one MAC/IP across epochs
residual_risk: platforms that do not randomize MAC addresses leave cross-epoch linkability by address

adversary: attacker of a single online release key or CI workflow; drift in the design ledger
asset: integrity of public binaries and of the proof obligations behind public claims
threat: a public binary or claim ships while its release gate is open, or a requirement is 'traced' to a conformance suite or gate that does not test it
residual_risk: the validator checks declared releases and registered suites, not whether an undeclared release is shipped

adversary: RecoveryRoot holder withholding a valid request
threat: withhold recovery from live controllers, wait elsewhere, then present an allegedly matured recovery
residual_risk: late/offline verifiers impose a fresh delay, reducing recovery availability

adversary: delayed/stale authorized reduction
threat: ABA: old revoke/remove targets a later re-add with the same semantic identity
residual_risk: implementations must preserve incarnation ids across materialization

adversary: first-contact identity substitution
threat: recipient accepts an intro identity that never proves the requester's stable AccountID before device sessions are established
residual_risk: human display-name impersonation remains addressed separately

adversary: malicious remote mini-app origin
threat: exfiltration after plaintext is posted into a foreign origin despite host-side network capability restrictions
residual_risk: any user-authorized remote disclosure gives that origin plaintext

adversary: untrusted SFU or non-joined Room endpoint
threat: feeding ciphertext to a silent listener that can derive Room-epoch exporter keys
residual_risk: joined participant endpoints can record/re-share media

adversary: implementation or formal-model drift
threat: two normative-looking encodings accept different controller/freeze transitions, allowing an implementation to authorize a child another verifier rejects
residual_risk: independent encodings can still contain the same conceptual bug; bidirectional equivalence and independent review remain required

adversary: malicious sender or caller-side integration bug
threat: an inbound PQXDH/Double-Ratchet envelope is accepted without, or under the wrong, relationship route and its IK is interpreted as the wrong peer
residual_risk: compromise or corruption of the already-trusted relationship state remains outside route-binding protection

adversary: provider or colluding provider roles; implementation that reintroduces account/device credentials for convenience
asset: metadata unlinkability and least-authority provider boundary
threat: routine provider administration is authenticated with AccountID/DeviceCredential/ACS material, creating unnecessary stable identity correlation or letting a provider become an account-authority verifier
residual_risk: provider-local resource handles still correlate operations on the same resource; IP/timing/size and same-operator role colocation remain observable

adversary: buggy issuer implementation, RNG failure or malicious issuance component
threat: Blind-RSA blinding factors are reused, allowing issuance transcripts to be matched to later redeemed tokens or batches
residual_risk: network timing, cardinality and endpoint metadata remain linkable outside the cryptographic property

adversary: over-privileged or colocated provider implementation
threat: a convenience role acquires identity, recovery, decryption or minting authority merely because interfaces or credentials expose powers unrelated to its function
residual_risk: arbitrary hostile code can violate local implementation boundaries; such an implementation is non-conformant and must not become a protocol root

adversary: malicious legacy guardian quorum, provider, or party supplying forged inactivity timestamps
asset: account continuity and prevention of false irreversible retirement
threat: a legacy claim is aged into terminal retirement using provider/guardian time, bypasses the owner inactivity/contest opportunity, or turns guardian credentials into general account authority
residual_risk: a valid malicious guardian threshold can force the account to remain in repeated/pending legacy attempts; it cannot skip verifier-local waits or gain other account powers

adversary: RecoveryStore operator, mailbox Home, or attacker with a provider-local record capability
asset: recovery privacy and least-authority recovery storage
threat: RecoveryRecord retrieval requires AccountID lookup or DeviceCredential auth, silently linking storage to identity; or possession of a record capability is treated as constitutional recovery authority
residual_risk: the RecoveryStore correlates accesses to the same opaque record and sees network/timing; mailbox Homes handling RecoveryRequest fan-out see AccountID for that operation

adversary: attacker exploiting advisory expiry/supersession semantics, compromised advisory issuer, or confused implementation
threat: an advisory expires, is superseded, or is user-overridden and the implementation interprets that event as permission to move an established relationship security floor backward
residual_risk: a user may consciously choose not to apply a non-threshold advisory's additional recommendation, but the relationship's stored historical floor and forbidden-profile rules still constrain the session

adversary: implementation author, parser differential attacker, or malicious peer exploiting schema drift
asset: canonical wire interpretation and signature/hash equivalence
threat: an implementation treats a permissive logical JSON schema as wire authority and accepts or interprets fields/extension semantics that are absent from the frozen CDDL/registries, producing cross-implementation parser or authorization divergence
residual_risk: non-W0/later-wave logical models can still evolve until their own wire freeze; implementations must identify the authoritative artifact for that object/version

adversary: malicious or stale KeyMaterialProvider, network cache, or restored client state
threat: an older still-valid signed AsyncKeyBundle is replayed after the peer has accepted a newer signed-prekey generation, steering establishment back to older or compromised signed-prekey material
residual_risk: a first observer that has never learned a newer generation cannot infer supersession from a malicious provider alone; expiry, device revocation and multi-provider comparison bound but do not eliminate that residual

adversary: malicious KeyMaterialProvider or party replaying signed public material
asset: one-time-prekey single-use context and session binding
threat: a valid one-time prekey is transplanted across devices, profiles, signed-prekey generations or provider pools because its signature authenticates only the standalone key item
residual_risk: a provider can still withhold or replay an already-consumed item to cause availability loss; the recipient device rejects consumed private-key ids

adversary: old backup, stale sync replica, or implementation merge bug
threat: restoring or merging stale relationship state lowers the highest accepted bundle generation and re-enables provider rollback
residual_risk: if every copy of a newer observation is lost, the client cannot cryptographically reconstruct it and must treat freshness as stale/first-observation state

adversary: web origin, reverse proxy, analytics pipeline, support tooling or log reader
threat: a capability leaks through a URL/query/cookie/referrer/cache/log/analytics/crash channel and is replayed as the holder
residual_risk: endpoint compromise can read capabilities in process memory; capability rotation/scope limits the resulting service authority but cannot make bearer theft harmless

adversary: malicious/stale RecoveryStore, cache or restored old backup
asset: fresh recovery routing/relationship metadata and rollback detection
threat: an older authenticated RecoveryRecord is replayed so a recovering client reuses obsolete routes/capabilities or forgets a newer observed ACS head
residual_risk: if every surviving copy of the newer record high-water state is lost, a recovering client cannot reconstruct that observation; authoritative ACS validation and provider revalidation still prevent the record itself from creating authority

adversary: attacker holding RecoveryRoot and RecoveryStore rendezvous
threat: the attacker derives normal-profile RecoveryRecord read/decryption material and learns relationship/provider metadata even though account activation is still delayed/vetoable
residual_risk: normal/recommended mode deliberately favors one-custodian usability; Maximum Privacy split custody protects relationship metadata only if the independent RelationshipRecoveryKey is not co-compromised

adversary: platform credential manager or correlated platform telemetry
threat: documentation treats random WebAuthn user.id as unlinkability even though RP ID and human user.name/recovery locator remain visible/correlatable
residual_risk: Recommended/Hardened synced-passkey custody intentionally exposes OM RP participation and recovery user metadata to the credential manager; Maximum Privacy avoids that platform custody

adversary: mailbox Home, relay operator, colocated provider roles or passive party reading provider-visible payload fields
asset: sender/relationship metadata privacy for established 1:1 delivery
threat: an established relay deposit exposes sender AccountID/DeviceID/identity key, Double Ratchet header or ConversationID because the inner envelope is sent without the ADR-0142 outer seal
residual_risk: source network address, timing, padding bucket, opaque queue/key identifiers, traffic volume and role colocation remain observable

adversary: malicious relay, stale peer or downgrade-prone implementation
threat: the sealed wrapper is stripped, unsupported, or a delivery key becomes unavailable and the implementation silently falls back to the pre-ADR-0142 clear-sender relay envelope
residual_risk: communication may fail until key/route refresh or peer software is updated; availability is preferred over silent privacy downgrade

adversary: malicious accepted contact, relay, stale queue or party replaying/transplanting valid outer ciphertext/key records
asset: delivery replay safety and relationship/device/route isolation
threat: a sealed wrapper is replayed for repeated effects, or a valid delivery-key record/wrapper is transplanted to another relationship/device/relay route
residual_risk: a legitimate accepted contact can consume its own scoped quota; route/timing correlation is not anonymity

adversary: confused implementation or malicious peer
threat: successful outer HPKE open is mistaken for sender authentication and bypasses RelationshipContext, ACS/DeviceCredential binding or inner ratchet validation
residual_risk: delivery-key public material is intentionally usable by the accepted peer; only the inner protocol authenticates which peer device authored the message

adversary: crash, storage fault, replaying peer or implementation with split persistence
asset: exactly-once authenticated sealed-delivery effects across crash
threat: outer replay reservation survives but inner session/dedupe acceptance or COMPLETE does not commit atomically, causing exact retry loss, duplicate inner effects, or cross-wrapper reuse under the same delivery key/id
residual_risk: storage exhaustion or persistent local corruption can cause fail-closed availability loss; the protocol does not promise progress when durable safety state cannot be maintained

adversary: malicious first-contact peer, confused implementation or copied pending-request state
asset: bootstrap capability isolation and pre-relationship authority boundary
threat: a MessageRequest reply_delivery_key is reused/transplanted across requests, profiles or routes, retained after bootstrap, or promoted into stable relationship state, enabling cross-request reflection/linkage or authority confusion
residual_risk: the accepting peer necessarily learns the request-scoped reply route/key after decrypting the MessageRequest; network/timing correlation is not eliminated

adversary: stale relationship state, delayed provider response or attacker exploiting update timing
asset: authenticated delivery availability without weakening device authorization
threat: a receiver treats temporarily stale or unavailable trusted peer ACS state as definitive inner-authentication failure, moves an otherwise valid RESERVED wrapper to REJECTED and permanently burns the exact retry before required monotonic head refresh
residual_risk: an unavailable authenticated ACS refresh can delay delivery until wrapper/key acceptance expiry; fail-closed availability loss is preferable to accepting under untrusted authority state

adversary: lost acknowledgement, crash, racing recipient devices or implementation with split bootstrap lifecycle persistence
asset: first-contact bootstrap liveness and single-branch relationship continuation
threat: a completed bootstrap private key is destroyed before an exact COMPLETE retry can be recognized, causing permanent lost-ack failure; or bootstrap acceptance/import/request closure commits non-atomically so two different valid recipient-device responses can create competing bootstrap branches after a race/crash
residual_risk: replay-only tombstones consume bounded local storage through the acceptance window; if required durable replay state is lost or corrupted, the endpoint fails closed rather than accepting a second bootstrap

adversary: racing recipient devices, local crash or implementation with non-atomic request closure
asset: bootstrap retry coherence and request-scoped key lifecycle
threat: a winning/terminal MessageRequest transition destroys the request-scoped private key while a losing RESERVED candidate remains resumable, leaving an unrecoverable key_missing_reserved state or permitting a stale terminal race to reopen/branch the bootstrap
residual_risk: a corrupted/lost durable request/replay database fails closed; it may lose availability but cannot authorize a second bootstrap

adversary: accepted-but-untrusted first-contact peer or permissive relay/provider
asset: bounded endpoint/provider replay storage and authority lifetime
threat: a peer exploits a physical-one-deposit interpretation of the reply route, creates unbounded distinct RESERVED candidates, or authenticates a wrapper expiry beyond its delivery-key/route/derived-bootstrap lifetime to pin durable replay state or extend acceptance beyond intended authority
residual_risk: an admitted peer may still consume up to the fixed eight-candidate budget and the configured acceptance window; provider-specific tighter quotas may reduce availability but not expand protocol authority

adversary: confused implementation or malicious first-contact peer exploiting divergent local lifetime policy
threat: two endpoints invent different independent request-expiry values for the same signed MessageRequest, so a wrapper is accepted by one implementation after another considers the request closed
residual_risk: ordinary wall-clock skew remains bounded by the frozen registry policy; cancellation/decline may intentionally close earlier

adversary: accepted-but-untrusted first-contact peer or implementation performing eager replay-record GC
threat: terminal candidate records are pruned while the request stays OPEN and their slots are reused, turning the nominal eight-candidate lifetime cap into an unbounded replenishable quota
residual_risk: the peer may still consume all eight slots and cause availability loss for later racing devices; that bounded exhaustion is intentional

adversary: stale historical backup, rollback or restore workflow
asset: first-contact cancellation/completion finality and bootstrap private-key retirement
threat: an old backup restores an OPEN/RESERVED MessageRequest, request-scoped private reply key or replay-only state and thereby reopens a cancelled/completed introduction or reactivates retired transport authority
residual_risk: restoring without pending bootstrap state may require a user to re-issue a still-desired introduction

adversary: local crash/reboot, malicious wall-clock change or stale timer backup
asset: recovery activation delay and controller veto opportunity
threat: a verifier credits unmeasured powered-off time or restored/wall-clock-derived elapsed time and accepts recovery earlier than the full verifier-local monotonic observation interval
residual_risk: conservative crash handling can delay legitimate recovery; reviewed secure monotonic hardware may safely reduce that availability penalty

adversary: malicious sender or divergent implementation exploiting presentation-extension registration/fallback ambiguity
threat: a standardized presentation extension is accepted on the wrong object/wrong criticality or a nonempty location fallback names a different point, so old and new clients authenticate/render different semantic content from the same ConversationEvent
residual_risk: sender-authored human labels may still be misleading, but they cannot replace the canonical coordinate-bearing point; malformed non-critical presentation metadata degrades to the W0 fallback

adversary: stale/offline/revoked endpoint, old backup or endpoint with badly skewed clock
asset: account-private draft/preference convergence without stale-state resurrection
threat: timestamp-only or arrival-order sync lets a far-future HLC pin state, an in-flight revoked record become effective, an offline branch resurrect a tombstoned item, or restored historical data be republished as if current
residual_risk: currently eligible same-account devices may intentionally make conflicting non-authoritative preference edits; causal merge may surface conflicts or prefer a deterministic tie-break, but cannot grant protocol authority

adversary: local race, OS callback, background task or confused client state during IdentityProfile switching
threat: an operation starts under profile A, the visible profile changes to B, and its asynchronous completion consults mutable global active-profile state and writes/displays A data in B
residual_risk: OS-global clipboard/push/provider resources can remain declared linkage/disclosure points; they are never treated as profile-private namespaces

adversary: compromised release signer/mirror or malicious metadata producer exploiting algorithm-agility ambiguity
threat: a verifier counts an allowed algorithm tag from an unauthorized/wrong-role key, double-counts duplicate signatures, substitutes key/algorithm under one key ID, signs different role/version bytes, or skips root-policy generations to satisfy a nominal threshold without authorized signing authority
residual_risk: compromise/coercion of enough currently authorized distinct threshold keys remains within the distribution's declared trust model; transparency is evidence/detection, not replacement authority

adversary: passive/active LAN observer, removed contact, malicious nearby peer or route-flapping network
asset: local-first availability without identity leakage, security downgrade or duplicate message state
threat: actual LAN delivery accidentally broadcasts stable identity, keeps relationship rendezvous alive after removal, treats a local endpoint as authority, performs unbounded unauthenticated work, or materializes a second message/file identity when WAN delivery/backfill later resumes
residual_risk: a contact explicitly enabled for local rendezvous can infer presence on a shared LAN; IP/link-layer observers still learn local traffic timing/topology, and locally delivered files may have reduced later availability until configured storage replication completes

adversary: malicious sender or divergent rich-text implementation
asset: cross-version authenticated text semantics and bounded rendering/resource use
threat: a list extension points at the wrong block, duplicates/out-of-order indexes, exceeds nesting/item limits, lies about ordered ordinals, or uses a fallback marker that differs from the richer rendering so old/new clients display materially different authenticated text
residual_risk: sender-authored list content itself may be deceptive and very long W0 content is still bounded by the ordinary RichText/event ceilings; malformed non-critical list metadata degrades to the readable fallback

adversary: implementation drift between PWA and native shells or platform capability assumption
asset: one interoperable V1 client semantics across web, Android and iOS
threat: a V1 feature silently depends on native-only background/local-network/key APIs or a native shell reimplements messaging/security meaning, causing protocol/UI behavior to diverge or web clients to claim capabilities the platform cannot supply
residual_risk: platform lifecycle and OS-policy differences remain real; V1 guarantees shared protocol/Core semantics and honest capability reporting, not feature-identical background behavior

adversary: holder of a stolen RecoveryRoot who can also advance a specific web verifier's system clock (for example via spoofed network time)
asset: verifier-local recovery-alone activation delay and the controller's veto window
threat: a Recommended-profile process_only verifier credits forged wall-clock gap time and accepts a recovery-alone successor before the legitimate controller's veto reaches it
residual_risk: limited to Recommended-profile web verifiers whose clock the adversary controls; a forward-only high-water blocks double credit and a mandatory authenticated veto sweep at acceptance still blocks any controller veto reachable through the account's routes; Hardened/Maximum verifiers are unaffected

adversary: malicious or buggy sender, or ordinary registry growth after clients ship
asset: convergent conversation state across client versions and across one account's own devices
threat: a crafted event carrying a schema-invalid payload for a newly registered non-critical extension is accepted by pre-registration clients and rejected by post-registration clients, or an edit leaves a stale location card/list interpretation, so devices materialize different conversations
residual_risk: future criticality downgrade is closed by ADR-0157/R-346 for the frozen V1 baseline; ordinary non-critical presentation divergence remains bounded by fallback semantics

adversary: passive observer on a shared or public LAN, or incompatible LAN implementations
asset: sender unlinkability and interoperable offline-local delivery
threat: a LAN binding carries the bare inner 1:1 envelope (sender EncodeEC(IK) in clear) or a stable per-device identifier, or two clients implement mutually unintelligible LAN protocols
residual_risk: timing, volume and IP/link-layer co-location remain visible; an explicitly LAN-enabled contact can infer presence, while identifiers/advertisements rotate and stay fixed-cardinality

adversary: schedule pressure or independent implementers
threat: a later-wave scope is authorized while its wire objects exist only as logical JSON schemas, so implementers invent incompatible encodings that later need a breaking migration
residual_risk: none architectural once the gate criteria hold; freeze quality still depends on independent review

adversary: malicious sender exploiting registry-version differences
asset: cross-version acceptance convergence for mandatory extension semantics
threat: a future critical extension is sent with critical=false so pre-registration clients accept it as unknown non-critical while newer clients reject the registered criticality mismatch
residual_risk: pre-V1 experimental implementations that do not implement the reserved prefix are outside the frozen V1 baseline; canonical registry governance still must not allocate non-critical meanings under the prefix

adversary: mixed-implementation account/group or incompatible client codec
threat: a GroupHistoryBundle is mistaken for implementation-private same-owner history, causing a newcomer to reject/misparse group history or lose the mandatory shared-by-bundle-author provenance boundary
residual_risk: bundle author can still lie about historical contents; the UI attributes the whole bundle to that author rather than authenticating claimed original authors

adversary: stale scheduled-send state after revocation, block, membership change or device-set change
asset: current authorization and recipient confidentiality at send time
threat: a client pre-encrypts or freezes recipients at schedule time and later releases ciphertext to a device/member/relationship that is no longer eligible
residual_risk: locally staged attachment material remains endpoint data until discarded; compromise of the scheduling device remains an endpoint threat

adversary: stale backup, compromised controller, or buggy client attempting to reuse a retired endpoint identity
threat: a DeviceID already in permanently_revoked_devices is linked again as messaging or control, resurrecting stale cryptographic/device state and creating an ABA path for old reductions or credentials
residual_risk: a fresh DeviceID on the same physical hardware is intentionally a new endpoint and must still complete ordinary enrollment/recovery checks

adversary: network reordering/partition, buggy client, or one eligible device publishing a competing availability update
asset: convergent delivery reachability and blob-location knowledge
threat: peers receive concurrent RelaySet or BlobLocationRecord updates in different orders and permanently choose different latest state, or a version jump/cross-lineage parent poisons the chain
residual_risk: an otherwise eligible compromised device can still publish bad-but-authorized availability metadata and cause bounded availability/privacy harm; it cannot create identity or content authority

adversary: malicious GroupHistoryBundle author or buggy group-history importer
asset: live Room event/control integrity and newcomer history provenance
threat: cross-Room/wrong-recipient history is accepted, or claimed historical EventIDs/control-like contents are fed into live Room reducers and suppress/replace/modify authenticated current state
residual_risk: the bundle author can still lie about historical content; the UI must continue attributing all imported history to that author rather than the claimed original sender

adversary: mixed-version implementations or a future profile with different one_to_one/group generation coordinates
asset: deterministic downgrade-floor semantics across account and Room state
threat: clients interpret ACS minimum_crypto_profile on different security_generation axes, so the same account transition is accepted as a raise by one implementation and rejected or treated as a downgrade by another
residual_risk: future profile registries must still assign per-conversation-type generations coherently; profile ids remain non-ordering allocation values

adversary: local profile confusion, telemetry shortcut or adaptive-ranking implementation bug
asset: IdentityProfile unlinkability and trustworthy navigation context
threat: Omnibar learning pools selections/queries across profiles, leaks local queries to a discovery provider while typing, or presents popularity/rank as identity confidence
residual_risk: a device-local attacker who can read an unlocked profile may infer local use patterns; OM does not claim local ranking state is secret from the endpoint owner/compromise

adversary: malicious theme bundle author
asset: filesystem/theme-sandbox integrity and semantic action/security UI
threat: a theme uses traversal/alias paths during extraction or supplies a deceptive icon asset to replace a reserved action/security glyph
residual_risk: media/font decoder defects remain possible despite allowlists/sanitization and require ordinary parser hardening/fuzzing before release

adversary: malicious or simply poorly designed theme, or active-speaker layout automation
asset: accessible, predictable user control and visual communication
threat: theme defaults override density/reduced-motion/alert policy, status becomes color-only, or active-speaker layout repeatedly displaces a participant the user pinned for visual communication
residual_risk: individual visual/cognitive needs vary; human accessibility/usability studies remain required before reference-client release

adversary: network failure, provider crash, or buggy retry implementation
asset: exactly-once logical user/control intent and convergent local state
threat: a mutation succeeds remotely but its acknowledgement is lost; the client reports rejection or invents a fresh operation id, causing duplicate messages/provider mutations/control effects after retry/restart
residual_risk: an external system without a usable idempotency/query mechanism may leave outcome genuinely unknown; OM must surface/reconcile that uncertainty rather than falsely claim exactly-once external effect

adversary: process crash, partition, or same-epoch competing group commit
asset: coherent MLS confidentiality state and Room authorization/materialization
threat: a client publishes or locally applies only one half of a GroupControlIntent/MLS Commit transition, sends application traffic on a tentative losing branch, or regenerates a different commit after lost acknowledgement, creating silent group-state/key divergence
residual_risk: the selected MLS runtime and persistence substrate still need V-004 formal/runtime evidence proving the journal can be implemented correctly under real crash/partition schedules

adversary: buggy or malicious implementation choosing a different validation/order sequence
threat: two implementations satisfy broad prose but differ in when they consume secrets, release plaintext, promote state or interpret an unknown outcome, creating security or interoperability divergence
residual_risk: independent review and implementation testing remain necessary

adversary: process crash, lost response or restart at an irreversible boundary
asset: authorization, dedupe, group state and provider mutation correctness
threat: a half-applied operation is replayed as a second semantic action, tentative group state becomes visible, or remote acceptance is mistaken for rejection
residual_risk: runtime crash/partition evidence remains open

adversary: registry-version skew or extension parser bug
threat: criticality/schema interpretation differs across client generations or logical schemas accidentally expand wire semantics
residual_risk: Rust/two-codec and independent compatibility evidence remains open

adversary: malicious local peer or history author
threat: LAN reachability or imported historical claims are mistaken for identity, membership, authorship or live control authority
residual_risk: real-LAN and group interoperability evidence remains open

adversary: mixed-version peers, downgrade attacker or implementation using numeric version ordering
asset: cross-version security negotiation and profile floors
threat: peers select different profiles or a lower-security profile because a higher numeric profile/version is mistaken for stronger security, bypassing the conversation-type security floor
residual_risk: future profiles must continue to receive coherent per-conversation security_generation assignments and independent negotiation evidence

adversary: malicious or buggy implementer mutating a published registry/profile/extension schema
asset: historical wire meaning and independent interoperability
threat: old and new implementations authenticate or materialize different semantics for the same published identifier because the old definition was silently changed in place
residual_risk: a fork can still deliberately diverge, but must preserve historical interpretation and publish a new lineage

adversary: future extension author or registry skew
threat: an extension version or criticality change makes one registry generation accept an object while another rejects or interprets it with different authority/security semantics
residual_risk: future registrations still require independent two-codec/interoperability evidence where their gate requires it

adversary: implementation agent optimizing for local test success or implementation convenience
asset: protocol design integrity and future agent consistency
threat: an agent labels a behavior-changing change as a clarification, edits a frozen schema/profile in place, or self-certifies local harness output as independent evidence
residual_risk: human/independent review is still required for external/formal/interoperability gates

adversary: thief holding one controller device of a two-controller account
asset: owner's continued control of the account
threat: the thief quarantines the owner's other device (or the owner suspends the stolen one), the account enters SAFETY_FREEZE, and a device-only freeze resolution needs the thief's cooperation, permanently locking the owner out
residual_risk: with recovery turned off a withholding controller can still deny resolution in a two-controller account; that is the explicit consequence of the no-recovery policy

adversary: later-wave registry change or implementation reading a shared registry
asset: frozen W0 wire validity and cross-version convergence
threat: a value added to a shared enum for a later wave (for example a new signature role) is accepted by W0 decoders on W0 objects, silently widening frozen W0 validity
residual_risk: new shared enums must keep using enum_value_waves; the validator and V-005 corpus catch the signature-role case

adversary: faulty CommitCoordinator
threat: the coordinator keeps a pending reduction from landing by publishing a non-reducing Commit at each new parent, or by equivocating with two Commits for one parent
residual_risk: a coordinator can still delay a reduction one epoch at a time by publishing its own reductions, which shrinks the roster each time; equivocation is ordered by the same key

adversary: member removed by the winning branch
asset: confidentiality of traffic sent on a losing branch
threat: a device removed on the winning chain keeps reading the losing branch's messages until that branch merges, because keeping reductions live under partition means a Commit is merged before it is confirmed
residual_risk: bounded by the partition duration plus sequencing_timeout; accepted as the price of reduction liveness and stated in the group security UX

adversary: member authorized for direct reductions
threat: the member publishes competing valid direct reductions to force repeated fork-and-recover cycles
residual_risk: each cycle costs one recovery Commit and gains no authority; the capability holder could already issue the reductions, and moderation can remove the abuser

adversary: member or faulty coordinator
threat: an author sets reducing=true on a non-reducing intent or binding to commit it directly after sequencing_timeout, or to outrank a coordinator-sequenced Commit at the same parent
residual_risk: for role.define, role.assign, admission.set, security_policy.set and governance.set the flag is recomputed against the parent state at apply time, which the wire checkers cannot do; the model and the conformance suite must cover that recomputation

adversary: state or platform gatekeeper
asset: availability and installability of OM clients
threat: a government or store operator orders removal of the app from a store or regional listing, or a native shell loads application code from a mutable origin that is then compromised or seized
residual_risk: the PWA origin and its hosting account remain a seizure and compromise point (ADR-0077); iOS offers no non-store native path outside regions with alternative distribution; Android developer verification may gate direct installs from 2027

adversary: attacker with a copy of the browser profile
asset: vault contents protected by a user passphrase
threat: offline guessing against the passphrase layer, or editing the stored KDF cost or salt to weaken or break unlock
residual_risk: no rate limiting exists offline; strength is the passphrase entropy times Argon2id cost; pure-JS Argon2id is slower than native; single-vendor review only until a pre-release cross-vendor read

adversary: remote holder of a public invite link
asset: the inviter device's CPU and attention
threat: floods first-contact requests so each costs an HPKE decapsulation and up to 65 chain links of composite-signature verification before any admission decision
residual_risk: per-profile limiter budget means one flooded link uses the budget of others; an attacker can keep the hourly budget exhausted; reserved invite-bound capacity and proof-of-work belong to a future IntroGate adapter

adversary: requester or introduction service
asset: a requester's AccountID privacy and the inviter's trust in an account
threat: reveals the requester's account to anyone holding a link before acceptance, or lets a self-presented chain stand in for an account the inviter never bound
residual_risk: the account named by the inviter's binding is trusted on first use at acceptance, like any first contact; the requester label is self-chosen and unverified

adversary: UI bug, learned suggestion or injected script
threat: dispatches a destructive intent with a forged, replayed or non-Core-issued confirmation token
residual_risk: a script running inside the same origin can still call the Core to obtain a nonce for a click it did not receive; the PWA origin remains an endpoint trust boundary

adversary: attacker with a cryptographically relevant quantum computer
asset: release-root trust (which online key may sign client updates)
threat: derives an Ed25519 root private key from its pinned public key, forges a 2-of-3 root delegation naming an attacker key and ships a malicious bundle
residual_risk: until a browser has accepted the pqRequired epoch (or runs a build with the build floor) an Ed25519-only chain is still accepted by it, so an attacker who can already forge Ed25519 roots can still serve that browser; the noble ML-DSA library is not independently audited (a second node:crypto implementation cross-checks it); an origin compromise that replaces sw.js bypasses the manifest entirely

adversary: operator error, vault loss or an attacker who strips or replays delegations
asset: availability and downgrade-resistance of the update chain
threat: loss of the PQ root key after clients hold the PQ floor strands them without updates, or a stripped or replayed Ed25519-only delegation downgrades a client that has not yet persisted the floor
residual_risk: there is deliberately no way to clear the floor: a lost PQ key (and no offline backup) means affected clients reinstall from an out-of-band release; the offline seed backup is a recommendation, not enforced
